summary: A Valkyrie steps on a polymorph trap. JavaScript preflight refuses POLY_TRAP, and its partial trap.c:trapeffect_poly_trap hero arm skips existing steedintrap and polyself implementations after removing the trap. Complete the whole source function and admit this branch, preserving monster behavior and the three hero branches for iron shoes, magic resistance or unchanging, and actual polymorph.

source.branch: trap.c:trapeffect_poly_trap (2453-2525) first marks and announces the trap. Hero iron shoes transform, Antimagic or Unchanging calls shieldeff and preserves the trap, and the ordinary branch calls steedintrap, deletes the trap, refreshes the square, then calls polyself(POLY_NOFLAGS). Monster arms handle iron shoes, magic resistance, and resisted or successful newcham.
callers: hack.c:spoteffects -> trap.c:dotrap -> trapeffect_selector -> trapeffect_poly_trap(hero); js/trap_effects.js preflight excludes POLY_TRAP before the already-partial hero arm.
trap.c:mintrap -> trapeffect_selector -> trapeffect_poly_trap(monster); preserve the existing JavaScript monster arms and their source return behavior.
dependencies: js/trap_effects.js already contains steedintrap and js/polyself.js exports polyself; replace the ordinary hero arm note_unported calls with source-ordered production calls and await their effects. The C discards both return values.
The Antimagic or Unchanging branch calls display.c:shieldeff and retains the trap; a separate v11 teleport investigation scopes that display helper. Preserve an exact void gap until it is ported.
The iron-shoes branch uses zap.c:poly_obj, update_inventory, and invent.c:prinv; verify existing partial code against C and remove placeholders when their source operations exist.
Shares js/trap_effects.js with assigned C41 fire-trap port; defer implementation until that reservation is released.
